holder_baseline.how_to_read: If the holder's own prior transactions are confirmed fraud, this holder identity is compromised: matching its baseline is evidence FOR fraud, not against it. A holder is defined by card, billing region and anchor day, so its history is always in its own region: whether the region is new can only be read at card level (alert_context.card_history.flagged_region_share_of_card).

shared_origin.how_to_read: lift = share of transactions on this element scoring >= 0.5, divided by the same share across all transactions. Large regions and common email domains carry many unrelated cards; a shared origin needs lift well above 1 and several distinct cards.

passages.text: of the SAR. The advisories and guidance can be found on FinCEN's website. 302 Refer to SAR Advisory Key Terms . Management’s primary focus should be on reporting suspicious activities, rather than on determining whether the transactions are in fact linked to money laundering, terrorist financing, or a particular crime. The following examples are red flags that, when encountered, may warrant additional scrutiny. The mere presence of a red flag is not by itself evidence of criminal activity. Closer scrutiny should help to determine whether the activity is suspicious or one for which there does not appear to be a reasonable business or legal purpose. Potentially Suspicious Activity That May Indicate Money Laundering Customers Who Provide Insufficient or Suspicious Information A customer uses unusual or suspicious identification documents that cannot be readily verified. A customer provides an individual taxpayer identification number after having previously used a Social Security number. A customer uses different taxpayer identification numbers with variations of his or her name. A business is reluctant, when establishing a new account, to provide complete information about the nature

assessment.reasoning: The alert was triggered solely by a real-time risk score of 0.71 on transaction 3640919 ($881.55). Customer ID C09241 represents an issuer bucket shared by multiple account holders, so normal behavior is assessed at the holder level (holder_id: C09241-K2|494|-43). The holder identity has zero prior transactions in confirmed fraud cases, indicating the identity is not compromised. Although the card experienced historical fraud between August and October 2016, those cases (such as CC-5469 and CC-5190) were initiated by customer reports of unauthorized activity rather than automated risk scores. In the current case, there is no customer dispute. Furthermore, the transaction occurred in-person in billing region 494, where the card has extensive history (491 prior transactions, representing 7.2% of card history, and six other transactions in the preceding 10-day window), refuting out-of-region card cloning. Shared origin analysis in region 494 shows zero hot transactions across 41 cards (lift 0.0). There is no card testing sequence (fits_card_testing_r5: false), no suspicious device involvement (in-person purchase, device null), and the card is not part of any fraud ring (ring_id: -1). Prior closed cases triggered by model scores on isolated high-value purchases of ~$850-$950 (CC-2956, CC-3092, CC-0339, CC-4158) were confirmed by cardholders and cleared. The evidence indicates this alert is a false alarm on legitimate cardholder spending.

report.summary: Transaction 3640919 ($881.55) on card C09241-K2 was alerted due to a legacy real-time risk score of 0.71. Investigation confirmed the transaction was conducted in person in billing region 494, an established home market accounting for 491 prior transactions and active recent spending. The cardholder has no record of confirmed fraud, no card testing patterns were observed, and the card is not linked to any fraud ring or suspicious devices. Precedent cases with similar model score alerts on comparable purchase amounts were verified as legitimate cardholder purchases. The alert is deemed a false alarm on legitimate cardholder activity, and the case is closed with no fraud.
report.stop_reason: The investigation ended pursuant to policy section 6 as the fraud probability of 0.083 is below the 0.15 threshold supported by six independent evidence bases, establishing decisive evidence of legitimate activity where further action would not change the outcome.
